title: Release Quarantine Windows & Escalation Playbook for Cross-Team Dependency Stabilization
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Purpose: establish a prescriptive set of 'quarantine windows' (timeboxed stabilization periods) and an associated escalation playbook to reduce cross-team release friction when interdependent work (eng, design, infra, security) is merging into a shared release lane.

Scope: quarterly releases and major patch windows where at least two teams own downstream contracts. This ticket covers cadence, signaling, automated readiness checks, security gating choreography, and a lightweight roll-forward/rollback decision tree. Does not include detailed infra automation tasks (those will be separate ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Documented quarantine window policy for minor/major release classes published in Confluence and linked in release checklists.
2) Standardized escalation matrix (roles + on-call contacts) for dependency blockers included in each release brief.
3) Automation hooks defined for readiness checks: test pass thresholds, SLO smoke checks, and security gating flags.
4) Pilot run during 2025-Q2 release with at least two cross-team dependencies using the playbook and retrospective notes.
5) Stakeholder sign-off from Eng, Design, Security, and Infra leads.
success_metrics:
- Reduce cross-team blocker count during 'hard freeze' by 40% for pilot release.
- Average time-to-resolution for cross-team dependency incidents falls from baseline 18h to <=8h.
- 80% of release briefs include validated readiness-check outputs before gating decision.
- Post-release retro shows actionable improvements and fewer rollback events (target: <1 per quarter for major releases).
risks:
- Teams may treat quarantine windows as rigid deadlines leading to rushed work and increased defects.
- Security gating can increase release latency if policies are not scoped with realistic SLAs.
- Lack of automation for readiness checks will create operational overhead for on-call and release coordinators.
- Ownership ambiguity for triage during the window (who is the 'owner' for cross-team escalations).
implementation_notes:
- Start with a lightweight policy: 48-hour quarantine window for patches, 72-96 hour for majors.
- Define 'readiness signals' (unit/integration pass rate, canary error rate threshold, infra quota checks, dependency-API contract validation).
- Security team to provide a minimal 'blocker' taxonomy (critical/major/minor) and expected turnaround SLAs for each.
- Release coordinator (rotating PM) responsible for running daily syncs during the window; an 'on-shift' engineer from each team listed in the escalation matrix.
- Build templated Slack channel naming and Confluence release brief template with a readiness checklist.
deploy_plan:
1) Week 1: Draft policy + checklist (contrib: PM, Eng, Security, Infra, Design).
2) Week 2: Iterate with teams and produce Confluence page + checklist template.
3) Week 3: Implement minimal automation hooks (scripts that pull build/test/canary status into the brief) — ENG follow-up tickets created.
4) Week 4: Pilot for Q2 minor release; collect metrics and retro.
5) Week 6: Adjust policy and roll out as org-wide recommendation for Q3.
